subject: Seat vs Consumption Uplift — options, billing impact, and legal considerations
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta@mindwave.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reed <tom@mindwave.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-contract uplift — seat vs consumption question

Neha —

Thanks for the quick sync yesterday. We dug into expected usage for Q3 and see a likely 40–60% spike driven by a new feature we plan to launch in July. Before we pull procurement in, wanted to clarify two things:

1) If we do a mid-contract uplift, is it possible to move from our current seat-based model to a hybrid (seats + consumption) without breaking the co-term?

2) What would a transition look like operationally (billing timing, invoicing, audits) — and are there any legal implications we should flag before taking this to our counsel?

I've attached an updated SOW with projected usage numbers. Tom is on the thread for procurement questions.

Best,
Marta
Head of Product, MindWave Labs

Attachments: MindWave_SOW_draft_v2.pdf

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Lopez <marta@mindwave.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Tom Reed <tom@mindwave.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-contract uplift — seat vs consumption question

Thanks Marta — appreciate the SOW and numbers. High level answers up front: yes, we can do a hybrid transition mid-contract and keep the co-term, but there are a few accounting and legal mechanics to align on (billing cadence for consumption, how overage/true-up is handled, and audit rights).

Operationally we typically support two common paths:

- Path A — "Top-up + Seat Hold": add a short-term consumption bucket for the spike (billed monthly) and keep seats unchanged; at renewal we convert realized consumption into a blended committed bucket if you want predictable unit pricing. Quick to stand up and minimizes legal churn.

- Path B — "Seat-to-Consumption Migration": formally convert a portion of seats to a consumption commitment (we'd amend the order form and pricing grid; billing moves to consumption-based invoices immediately, but co-term is preserved). This requires a one-off amendment and finance sign-off; it can change audit/usage reporting slightly.

Action items for us to proceed:
1) Jordan — can you confirm indicative blended unit pricing for a 40–60% uplift (monthly consumption over next 3 months) and a temporary 10% discount window for committed conversion?
2) Kimberly — ops: what's the shortest lead time to enable a consumption bucket for MindWave and any onboarding checklist?
3) David — legal/finance: flag any billing or audit clauses that would need explicit amendment for Path B (especially around consumption reconciliation windows).

Marta/Tom — if you can confirm which path you prefer (fast top-up vs conversion), we'll draft a concise amendment and an invoice example so procurement has something to review.

Thanks — Neha
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-pricing-grid.xlsx

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marta Lopez <marta@mindwave.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Tom Reed <tom@mindwave.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-contract uplift — seat vs consumption question

Marta — quick notes on pricing options. I modeled a few scenarios against your projected tokens (thanks for the SOW):

- Temporary consumption bucket (Path A): we can set a short-term bucket for 3 months at a blended unit rate that's ~8% below list consumption pricing (volume-backed). No change to current seats; invoiced monthly.

- Commit conversion (Path B): if MindWave converts >=25% of current seats into a 12-month committed consumption tranche, we can offer a conversion credit equal to 2 months of current seat spend (applied to the first invoice) plus a 12% blended discount on committed units. This requires an amendment and finance approval, but keeps co-term intact.

- Expedited option: if procurement signs within 10 business days, extend the conversion credit to 3 months of seat spend (one-time).

I'll attach an illustrative pricing table (see redwood-pricing-grid.xlsx Neha attached). Neha — if MindWave prefers Path B, I'll prepare a priced amendment draft for legal to review.

-Jordan
Senior Account Strategist, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Lopez <marta@mindwave.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-contract uplift — seat vs consumption question

Marta/Tom — ops details:

- Path A (consumption bucket) lead time: 3 business days to provision, 1 business day to test; monthly invoicing, with a consumption ledger exported to your finance SFTP or pulled via our billing API. No change to existing IAM.

- Path B (migration): legal amendment + PO update; lead time typically 7–10 business days once signed. Billing-wise we'll switch the converted portion to consumption invoices effective the amendment date. Reconciliation: we run a 14-day reconciliation window at month-end for any overage/underconsumption adjustments.

Operational ask for procurement: preferred invoicing cadence (monthly vs net30 consolidated), and whether you need detailed per-route token breakout in the invoice.

Kimberly
Senior Ops Manager, Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marta Lopez <marta@mindwave.ai>, MindWave Legal <legal@mindwave.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-contract uplift — seat vs consumption question

Folks — quick legal/finance note. Path A is low friction from a contract perspective; we can do it under existing SOW with a short Order Form addendum that covers the bucket size, unit price, and invoicing cadence. No changes to audit rights.

For Path B we need to amend the Order Form and the Billing Schedule: specifically call out reconciliation windows (we recommend 14 days), early termination math for the converted committed tranche, and clarify whether the conversion credit is refundable or non-refundable (we typically apply it as a credit against your first consumption invoices).

Marta/legal: two items we typically see customers ask:
1) Audit clause — if you need more frequent usage exports for internal compliance, we can include a clause for monthly exports (ops will set up SFTP/API).
2) Data residency/processing — no change from current terms, but if you need additional contractual guarantees for logs retention we can add a short addendum.

If MindWave wants Path B, please get procurement and legal eyes on the priced amendment; Jordan and I will coordinate the language. If you want to move quickly without legal review, Path A is the recommended route.

-David
Head of Finance & Legal Ops, Redwood Inference
